How does '107. One last recollection of the Dhamma' present the dynamics of Dependent Arising (paṭiccasamuppāda)?

The text explains: *"Then he told them to chant the Sati-sambojjhaṅga Sutta three times, and Dependent Co-arising three times."* Dependent Arising demonstrates how ignorance (*avijjā*) triggers mental concocting (*saṅkhāra*), leading to consciousness, sensory contact, feeling, and craving. When ignorance is replaced by direct knowing through insight (*paññā*), the entire chain of conditional suffering uncouples in reverse (*paṭiloma*), revealing the unconditioned Nibbāna.

How does '107. One last recollection of the Dhamma' characterize the nature of consciousness and the knowing mind?

The text observes: *"Then he asked us to chant the Great Establishings of Mindfulness (Mahā Satipaṭṭhāna) Discourse, but none of us had memorized it."* Consciousness (*viññāṇa*) is not an independent 'soul' or enduring self; it arises in dependence on contact (*phassa*) and sense objects. The practice is to distinguish between the passing objects of awareness (thoughts, feelings, sensations) and the pure, unattached quality of 'the one who knows' (*poo roo*), resting in unconditioned peace.
